required_source.premise_used: A genuine rank-two projection Z=C^T X of independent cap-one original coordinates satisfies ||p_Z||_infinity<=2/sqrt(det(C^T C)); projected coordinates need not be independent.

partner_result.application: Compared the valid square-peel plus in-range rank-two half-Riesz certificate against a definite projected-pair route on a nonzero near-null N3 family; Schur-first gives 16 sqrt(30)|delta|^(-1/4)(2+delta)^(-1/4), while conditioning the original hub first gives 2 pi.

mathematical_result.theorem: For any R^2-valued Z with joint density cap M and any definite symmetric 2x2 B, Z^T B Z + ell^T Z + c has essential density at most pi M/sqrt(det|B|). For a genuine product projection Z=C^T X_L this gives 2 pi/sqrt(det(C^T C) det|B|), uniformly after conditioning disjoint original-coordinate variables that only create affine terms.
mathematical_result.sharp_interface: The same cap-only receiver abstraction fails for every fixed invertible indefinite quadratic Hessian via a cap-one hyperbolic-strip law with output peak log R, and fails for rank-one semidefinite curvature via square-root singularity.
mathematical_result.target_valid_application: For Q_delta=delta X_0^2+2 sqrt(2(1+delta)) X_0 Y+Y^2+Z^2 with balanced orthonormal product-projection leaves Y,Z and delta>-1, the nonzero spectrum is {delta+2,-1,1}; for nonzero |delta| below any N3 threshold and sufficiently large leaf bank, all physical diagonals and pair determinants are below threshold, yet ||p_Qdelta||_infinity<=2 pi for arbitrary independent cap-one input laws.
mathematical_result.independence_scope: Only independence of disjoint original-coordinate groups is used. The two projected leaf coordinates may be dependent throughout.

unresolved_implication: Close the indefinite near-null / overlapping-product-provenance receiver with a source invariant stronger than the projected density height, retaining arbitrary additional spectrum and avoiding singular Schur-first inversion.
next_step: Seek a product-provenance half-Riesz or mixed-Fresnel inequality for an indefinite two-dimensional projected receiver coupled to the original scalar hub, with constants stable as the scalar pivot tends to zero.
